answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the jetty index resolves every citation against the plume checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the comet audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 93 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 93 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 15 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
